title: Inhomogeneous Wu–Wang produces a third coefficient that two-log Juggler finance cannot see
statement: An exact CycleMin identity produces a Wu–Wang form |p + b log 2 + c log 3| with a nonzero integer p that is forced smaller than the homogeneous Lambda = o log 3 - L log 2, so the linear-independence measure for 1, log 2, log 3 squeezes a leftover that the two-log finance reduction leaves standing.
mathematical_domain: Juggler cycle finance / linear forms in 1, log 2, log 3
tested_range: unscaled p in [-5,5] and k-clearing on leftover seeds 19, 84, 569, 1054, 25781, 50508, 176251
counterexamples: global_defect_identity / image_eq_start_defectRatio give log R = G log n, not an integer; the exponent-budget sum is exactly Lambda (p = 0)
on all seven seeds, min_{p≠0} |p+Lambda| = 1-Lambda (equality at p = -1), so every unscaled inhomogeneous form is order 1

at L=19, clearing k=74 gives |k Lambda-1|=2.776e-3 against a diagnostic Wu-Wang floor ~1.1e-13 (ratio 2.52e10); at L=176251 the ratio is 1.20e38. Choosing k after the fact is the same Lambda, not a forced second form
notes: The integer 1 in Wu–Wang is the real number 1, not a floor remainder. Attack C already used the p=0 corollary as a fan-width cap. Baker leftover-killer stays REFUTED. Not a halt theorem.
